7 / 33

The Important Distinction

Automation is what every other vendor uses. AI is what we use.

A really important thing to remember before we go deeper.

Automation

What every other vendor uses.

A customer goes in. The customer gets a text. That's it. One-way. Blast. Same message to everyone, regardless of who they are or where they came from.

  • One-way messaging
  • Blanket sequences
  • No context awareness
  • No escalation, no handoff
AI

What we invest in.

Two-way intelligent conversation. The system understands what the customer is saying, asks the right questions back, books the appointment, and escalates to a human only when the moment calls for it.

  • Two-way conversation, real responses
  • Source-aware: HD customer gets a different message than D2D
  • High-intent escalation ("leak" → emergency)
  • Hands off to a live human when warm
For Home Depot: when we use the word automation, we mean automation. When we say AI, we mean AI. We are invested in AI — and that's the experience Home Depot's customers get.

Customer Portal · Service

Service requests — AI answers immediately.

When a customer files a service request, our AI responds immediately. The customer knows they were heard. They get a response timeline. For an emergency, they're told someone will contact them within 30 minutes. That's the only thing they care about.

My kitchen faucet is leaking — water everywhere.
Got it, Linda — we hear you. A service technician will contact you within 30 minutes. We've also alerted our service manager directly.
Pablo is on the way. ETA 27 minutes.
The customer hears back immediately.
They know the claim was heard. They know someone is responding. That's the only thing the customer cares about.
Emergencies get a 30-minute response window.
If the AI hears "leak" or "flood" — the service manager is notified directly and the customer sees the timeline in real time.
Internal priority is handled by us.
The system tags every request internally as routine, two-hour, or emergency. The customer never sees that classification. They only see action.
